item.title: [9] A B1g phonon unlocks d-wave superconductivity in the repulsive Hubbard model
item.description:
Last authors: Zhi-Xun Shen, Thomas P. Devereaux

Authors: Wen O. Wang, Tianshu Li, Xiaoyue Ma, et al.

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: author whitelist: Zhi-Xun Shen

Tags: #STS #superconduct #correlated #Hubbard #phonon

Abstract: Using numerically exact finite-temperature quantum Monte Carlo, we demonstrate that a $B_{1g}$ phonon coupled to the doped $t$-$t'$ repulsive Hubbard model produces genuine $d$-wave superconductivity at a substantial transition temperature, in excess of either interaction alone. The observed trends suggest that stronger Hubbard repulsion may cooperate with the phonon to further raise the pairing scale. The enhancement persists at stronger repulsion within the accessible window, limited by the fermion sign problem, and follows a common trend across phonon frequencies $\Omega$ when organized by a retardation scale $2\pi T/\Omega$. We also find a well-defined superconducting dome in doping, echoing a characteristic feature of correlated superconductors. Our results identify the $B_{1g}$ phonon as a plausible microscopic ingredient for robust $d$-wave superconductivity in the Hubbard model and suggest a concrete, physically motivated route toward materials with higher superconducting transition temperatures.

item.title: [8] Meta-Altermagnetism and Enhanced Spin-Splitting
item.description:
Last authors: Bogeng Wen, Hae-Young Kee

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Relevant theoretical development for altermagnetism and spin-splitting bands in 2D systems.

Tags: #altermagnet #spin-splitting #theory

Abstract: Altermagnets are collinear magnets with zero net magnetization and spin-split electronic bands. Here, we explore whether altermagnetism can exhibit a discontinuous jump, a phenomenon we refer to as meta-altermagnetism. We show that meta-altermagnetism can emerge in 2D systems when magnetic-order-induced band reconstruction drives spin-split van Hove singularities (vHSs) across the Fermi level. Using mean-field theory for an extended $t$-$J$ model on a two-sublattice square lattice including anisotropic hopping integral, we find that a first-order meta-altermagnetic transition produces an intermediate altermagnetic regime with reduced staggered magnetization but strongly enhanced magnetic octupole and time-reversal-odd spin-splitter conductivity. We further show that the first-order transition line terminates at a quantum critical endpoint, giving rise to a rich phase diagram as the chemical potential and anisotropic hopping strength are varied. Our results identify the spin split vHSs as a route to enhancing spin-splitter effect for spintronic applications.

item.title: [9] Evidence for a charged vortex lattice in an exciton superfluid
item.description:
Last authors: Allan MacDonald, Ali Yazdani

Authors: Ryan L. Lee, Jungwoo Lee, Viliam Va\v{n}o, et al.

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: author whitelist: Ali Yazdani

Tags: #graphene #superconduct #Landaulevel

Abstract: Lattices of quantized vortices are a defining property of rotating superfluids and of type-II superconductors in magnetic fields. Realizing an analogous vortex lattice in an exciton superfluid-formed from bound electron-hole pairs-has remained challenging because excitons are electrically neutral. Building on previous theoretical studies of the low-energy excitations in an exciton superfluid, recent theory has predicted that in a strong magnetic field, a weakly charged exciton superfluid can stabilize a vortex-antivortex lattice arising from the mutual repulsion of fractionally charged vortex cores. Here we report evidence for this predicted vortex lattice in a bilayer exciton condensate by imaging its charged vortices with the scanning tunnelling microscope. The condensate forms between Landau levels of two graphene layers separated by a thin hexagonal boron nitride barrier in a perpendicular magnetic field. We find that the vortex lattice periodicity scales with the total excess charge and is insensitive to its distribution between the two layers, in quantitative agreement with theoretical predictions. Our observations provide evidence for phase coherence in an exciton superfluid system.

item.title: [7] Few-Electron Partitioning in the Fractional Quantum Hall Regime
item.description:
Last authors: J. Rech, B. Gr\'emaud

Authors: T. Jonckheere, J. Rech, B. Gr\'emaud

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Fractional quantum Hall physics with potential experimental observation relevance.

Tags: #quantumHall #fractionalquantumHall

Abstract: Motivated by few-electron partitioning experiments [Shaju et al., Nature 642, 928 (2025)], we study the partition statistics of $N$-electron states at a fractional quantum Hall point contact. At the solvable point $g=1/2$, we obtain nonperturbative current and noise formulas for arbitrary drives, while for Lorentzian pulses (Levitons) the full counting statistics reduces to an $N\times N$ determinant. We show that the charge is transferred solely in units of $e$, and that symmetrized cumulants for $N=2,3,4$ reveal strong antibunching and higher-order correlations, observable in a $(\nu_1,\nu_2)=(1,1/3)$ junction.

item.title: [8] From a Lifshitz Transition to Spin-Density-Wave Order: Sr2RuO4 under Uniaxial Strain
item.description:
Last authors: Maria Chatzieleftheriou, Antoine Georges

Authors: Evgeny A. Stepanov, Sophie Beck, Maria Chatzieleftheriou, Antoine Georges

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Electronic structure study of a landmark correlated material under strain.

Tags: #superconduct #Fermisurface #Sr2RuO4

Abstract: In recent years, the effects of uniaxial strain on Sr$_2$RuO$_4$ have been extensively investigated, revealing a pronounced enhancement of the superconducting critical temperature accompanied by experimental indications of an emergent magnetically ordered state. In this Letter, we study the impact of strain on the spectral and magnetic properties of this material within an advanced many-body theoretical framework. We find that strain induces an anisotropic Lifshitz transition, which enhances the electron scattering rate along the elongation axis while simultaneously promoting coherent Fermi-liquid behavior in the perpendicular direction, in close agreement with experimental observations. Taking into account this anisotropic behavior allows us to capture the magnetic instability leading to a finite-temperature ordered state at large strain values. Our analysis further reveals that the magnetic response is dominated by two competing wave vectors associated with distinct nesting vectors: one within the $\gamma$ sheet and the other between the $\alpha$ and $\beta$ sheets of the Fermi surface. Both wave vectors can stabilize magnetic order, with their competition depending sensitively on the coherence of the respective Fermi surface sheets.

item.title: [9] Incoherent dark excitons extend Floquet-like physics across time and momentum
item.description:
Last authors: Gianluca Stefanucci, Keshav M. Dani

Authors: Xing Zhu, Jacques Hawecker, Enrico Perfetto, et al.

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Direct TR-ARPES observation of long-lived Floquet-like physics in 2D heterostructures.

Tags: #angle-resolvedphotoemission #photoemission #heterostructure #Floquet

Abstract: Floquet phenomena - where a coherent, time-periodic drive hybridizes the conduction band with energy-replicated copies of the valence band - have been demonstrated with intense optical fields and, more recently, other bosonic excitations. However, within mean-field approximations and the current understanding of Floquet phenomena, these effects survive only for the coherence time of the drive, limiting practical use and current demonstrations to the sub-picosecond regime. Here, consistent with recent theoretical predictions beyond the mean-field picture, using time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy in WSe$_2$/MoS$_2$ heterostructures, we show that incoherent, dense populations of dark interlayer excitons hybridize the conduction band with energy-replicated copies of the valence band, mimicking Floquet-like phenomena - now persisting for nearly a nanosecond. With increasing interlayer exciton density, the valence band and its replica evolve from an inverted-parabolic to a Mexican-hat dispersion, a signature of the predicted non-zero static coupling that hybridizes the bands and scales linearly with the exciton density. By tuning twist angle, we further show that dark excitons with net momentum create replicas that hybridize with bands offset not just in energy but also in momentum, providing another powerful degree of freedom beyond conventional Floquet engineering. These results establish a robust, long-lived route to engineering electronic states, beyond a coherent, zero-momentum drive.

item.title: [8] Charge Filling-Dependent Valley Polarization and its Dynamics Driven by Correlated Interlayer Exciton States in WSe2/WS2 Heterobilayer
item.description:
Last authors: Takashi Taniguchi, Kazunari Matsuda

Authors: Zhiwei Li, Haonan Wang, Yubei Xiang, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Important study on correlated states and excitons in moiré heterostructures.

Tags: #heterostructure #correlated #Mott #phonon

Abstract: Moir\'e heterostructures of transition metal dichalcogenides provide an emerging platform for studying the strongly correlated electronic and excitonic states. The valley degree of freedom and its dynamics in the strongly correlated electronic and excitonic states in the moir\'e system are crucial for fundamental understanding and applications of valleytronics. Although the strongly correlated states in moir\'e systems have been extensively investigated, their impact on valley degrees of freedom and its dynamics remains unexplored. Here, we study the charge filling-dependent valley relaxation dynamics of interlayer excitons (IXs) in WSe2/WS2 moir\'e heterobilayer system. The evolution of moir\'e IXs dynamics across the Mott transition is elucidated by combining time-resolved optical spectroscopy with Monte Carlo simulation. Our results show that the radiative decay and recombination rate of IXs are enhanced at the integer filling factors n (=-1). Moreover, the valley relaxation rate of IXs at n=$\pm$1 is significantly decreased. The resulting reduction in wavefunction overlap and phonon scattering process suppresses the nonradiative recombination and intervalley scattering of IXs. These anomalous behaviors are attributed to the modification of IXs recombination pathways and enhance excitonic coherence due to the localization of introduced charge carriers at integer filling of moir\'e site. Our results explore exciton and valley dynamics as sensitive probes of strongly correlated states in moir\'e systems and highlight possible ways to control excitonic coherence and valleytronic properties in two-dimensional quantum materials.

item.title: [8] The Flexoelectric Twist: Persistence of Heavy Fermion Picture in Small-Angle Twisted Bilayer Graphene
item.description:
Last authors: Xi Dai, Berthold J\"ack

Authors: Qirong Yao, Ka Cheuk Fan, Tianyu Qiao, Hao Shi, Xi Dai, Berthold J\"ack

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: STM study of correlated physics in twisted bilayer graphene, relevant to moire systems and flat bands.

Tags: #STS #graphene #twistedbilayer #correlated

Abstract: Twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) near the first magic angle ($\theta\approx1.05^{\circ}$) hosts flat bands that provide a fertile ground for exploring strongly correlated and topological phases. At smaller twist angles ($\theta<1^{\circ}$), attice relaxation profoundly alters the moir\'e landscape. The extent to which moir\'e lattice reconstruction at different length scales affects the electronic structure through electro-mechanical coupling remains unresolved. Here, using scanning tunneling microscopy on small-angle TBG devices ($\theta\approx0.3-0.7^{\circ}$), we observe a pronounced $dI/dV$ peak at the AA site of the moir\'e lattice on top of a spectrum that is asymmetric about the charge neutrality point, lattice reconstruction over moir\'e lattice length scales, as well as a dilation of the atomic lattice at the AA sites. We demonstrate at a phenomenological level that the inclusion of moir\'e lattice reconstruction supports compact localized heavy fermion $f-$ states localized at AA sites. The additional inclusion of atomic lattice dilation enerates a strong flexo-electric response that explicitly breaks particle-hole symmetry, pushing compact, localized $f$-states at the AA sites down in energy. Consequently, these heavy fermion states energetically coexist with itinerant $c$-electrons at the AB/BA sites. Our spatially resolved spectroscopic measurements quantitatively visualize this coexistence, confirming the persistence of the heavy fermion model in the small-angle regime $\theta<1^{\circ}$. Our findings provide microscopic insights into how flexo-electricity affects the low-energy electronic structure of small-angle TBG. More broadly, our study establishes small-angle TBG as a new class of moir\'e materials to explore the interacting Kondo lattice problem with high tunability of the $f-$occupation and $c-$density through twist-angle and electrostatic back gates, respectively.

item.title: [9] Direct real-space imaging of sign-reversal superconducting state by scanning Josephson tunneling
item.description:
Last authors: Ziqiang Wang, Jian Wang

Authors: Tianheng Wei, Yanzhao Liu, Wei Ren, Zhen Liang, Ziqiang Wang, Jian Wang

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Direct visualization of pairing symmetry in iron-based superconductors using SJTM, high relevance to spectroscopy.

Tags: #superconduct #STS #spectroscopy

Abstract: Phase-sensitive experiments based on Josephson tunneling have been considered as a pivotal method to determine the pairing symmetry in high-temperature (high-Tc) cuprate superconductors. However, in iron-based superconductors, traditional phase-sensitive experiments face setbacks because of the complexity of pairing symmetry in multiband systems. Here, using scanning Josephson tunneling microscopy (SJTM), we report the half-unit-cell periodic Josephson tunneling modulations in monolayer high-Tc Fe(Te,Se) film epitaxially grown on SrTiO3(001). The Josephson tunneling almost vanishes along the lines connecting next-nearest-neighbor Fe atoms under an s-wave superconducting tip. Combined with single-particle tunneling spectra showing the full superconducting gap, our experimental results are consistent with the sign-reversal nodeless d-wave pairing symmetry. Our findings provide sub-unit-cell scale superconducting phase information for understanding the mechanism of high-Tc superconductivity. We anticipate our work as a starting point for atomically resolved Josephson interference experiments using SJTM in various unconventional superconductors.

item.title: [8] Layer-Parity Control of the Superconducting Diode Effect in Monolayer NbSe2
item.description:
Last authors: Yusuf Wicaksono, Toshikaze Kariyado

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical exploration of the superconducting diode effect in NbSe2, relevant to 2D materials and proximity.

Tags: #monolayer #superconduct #NbSe2

Abstract: The superconducting diode effect is often associated with finite-momentum pairing, although model studies indicate that rectification reflects the asymmetry of the free energy about its minimum rather than the equilibrium pair momentum itself. Using a Wannier-based, self-consistent finite-$\mathbf Q$ Bogoliubov-de Gennes approach with a Fermi-surface-adaptive quadrature that converges the critical currents, we show that the layer parity and orientation of magnetic proximity select the diode response of monolayer NbSe$_2$. For in-plane exchange, the equilibrium pair momentum $\mathbf Q_{\rm eq}$ and the diode efficiency are both linear in the layer-odd exchange contrast: parallel proximity on the two Se sublayers is reciprocal, and antiparallel proximity doubles the response. An out-of-plane component separates the two observables. It leaves $\mathbf Q_{\rm eq}$ nearly unchanged but, through pair breaking, suppresses the efficiency by more than an order of magnitude and, at low temperature, reverses it. Purely out-of-plane exchange, for which $C_3$ symmetry forbids a helical term, keeps $\mathbf Q_{\rm eq}=0$ yet produces a trigonal diode effect, controlled by the layer-even exchange and larger than the in-plane one above $0.65$~meV at low temperature. Magnetic layer parity thus selects between a helical and a trigonal diode channel. The trigonal channel is an intrinsic, symmetry-allowed contribution to the field-free rectification reported in NbSe$_2$/CrBr$_3$ and predicts that two-sided out-of-plane proximity cancels it when antiparallel and, at the same exchange per layer, enhances it about fourfold when parallel, in the computed range.

item.title: [8] Two-Dimensional Magnetic Materials from Ferromagnetism to Altermagnetism: Fabrication, Symmetry, Evidence, and Device Readiness
item.description:
Last authors: Peixin Qin, Zhiqi Liu

Authors: Guojian Zhao, Ziang Meng, Li Liu, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Comprehensive review of 2D magnets and altermagnets, directly relevant to magnetic topological materials research.

Tags: #altermagnet #monolayer #magnetism

Abstract: Atomically thin magnets are governed by composition, thickness, stacking, strain, defects, substrates, ferroic order, and interfaces. This Review organizes two-dimensional (2D) magnetism using net magnetization and momentum-space spin splitting or spin-polarization patterns as primary coordinates, supplemented by sublattice structure and the symmetry relations between opposite-spin sublattices. Ferromagnets generally carry a net moment; ferrimagnets can be fully compensated. Conventional antiferromagnets may retain spin-degenerate bands, while altermagnets permit nonrelativistic alternating spin splitting under dimension-specific symmetry constraints. M1-M4 reporting classes introduced here distinguish layer-resolved atomically thin forms, non-layer-resolved thin flakes or films, bulk benchmarks, and theoretical candidates or design routes; the evidence category and ordering-temperature provenance are reported independently. Current experimental support for altermagnetism comes mainly from M2 thin-film and M3 bulk benchmarks, leaving a fully verified atomically thin M1 altermagnetic phase as an open experimental goal. Most proposed monolayer and few-layer systems therefore fall within M4, and contested cases clarify the measurements needed for phase assignment. Device readiness is compared qualitatively using operating temperature, readout, switching, domain control, stability, scalability, interface sensitivity, and integration difficulty. Reliable phase assignment and device assessment require complementary measurements from the same material form under matched conditions, ideally on the same specimen or in situ.

item.title: [9] Giant piezomagnetic response driven by spin reorientation in the topological Kagome magnet TbMn6Sn6
item.description:
Last authors: Juntao Huo, Guowei Li

Authors: Hanyang Qian, Wen Sun, Juntao Huo, Guowei Li

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental investigation of magnetic kagome systems with topological implications.

Tags: #kagome #topological #magnetism

Abstract: Achieving a large strain response to a small magnetic-field variation remains a challenge in magnetomechanical materials, particularly in topological systems where the coupling between spin reconstruction and lattice deformation remains unclear. Here, we report an anomalous magnetostrictive response associated with field-induced spin reorientation in the topological Kagome magnet TbMn6Sn6. Below its spin-reorientation temperature of 310 K, an in-plane magnetic field induces an abrupt increase in magnetostriction, which exceeds 120 ppm at 240 K. This transition produces a giant differential piezomagnetic coefficient of approximately 5000 ppm T-1, far exceeding the values reported for other topological magnetic materials and commercial FeGa alloys, and placing TbMn6Sn6 among the most field-sensitive magnetostrictive materials. The field position of this peak agrees with the anomalies in magnetization and magnetotransport, demonstrating that the large differential response is tied to field-induced spin reorientation. Thermal expansion also changes across the spin-reorientation boundary. Raman measurements reveal corresponding anomalies in phonon energy and linewidth, indicating that the reorientation modifies the lattice dynamics. The combined results support a mechanism in which competing magnetic anisotropies of the Tb and Mn sublattices, coupled through Tb-Mn exchange, create magnetic configurations with different equilibrium strains. This finding establishes spin reorientation as a route to giant piezomagnetic responses in topological magnets and provides a basis for magnetomechanical sensing and switching near room temperature.

item.title: [7] Collective sliding relaxor ferroelectricity across thousand-layer van der Waals superstructures
item.description:
Last authors: Kaihui Liu, Zhipei Sun

Authors: Nianze Shang, Cuiju Yu, Yucai Lin, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of novel sliding ferroelectricity in van der Waals structures.

Tags: #vanderWaals #experimental

Abstract: Relaxor ferroelectrics are among the most important electromechanical materials owing to their exceptionally large electrostrictive responses. However, conventional relaxor behavior is generally associated with chemical complexity and structural disorder, where local compositional fluctuations generate polar nanoregions, making the microscopic origin of this behavior difficult to control and engineer. Here we report sliding relaxor ferroelectricity (S-RFE), a previously unknown relaxor state in which engineered stacking-phase heterogeneity enables cooperative interlayer sliding to generate collective relaxor behavior. Through stacking-phase engineering in rhombohedral boron nitride, we create sliding domains that act as structural analogues of polar nanoregions and cooperatively align under an electric field through interlayer sliding. This collective state produces reversible electromechanical deformation of up to approximately $-1.6\%$ with negligible hysteresis in approximately 300-nm-thick crystals, corresponding to approximately 1000 atomic layers. The resulting electrostriction coefficient ($Q_{33}$ of approximately $1200\,\mathrm{m}^{4}\mathrm{C}^{-2}$) exceeds those of most crystalline electrostrictors by orders of magnitude. item.title: [9] Separating the Density Wave Phase from Zero-Resistance Superconductivity in La4Ni3O10
item.description:
Last authors: Y. E. Suyolcu, B. Keimer, H. Takagi, P. Reiss

Authors: P. Puphal, A. Suthar, B. Wehinger, V. Sundaramurthy, T. Priessnitz, M. Knauft, et al.

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Direct experimental study of nickelate superconductivity and density waves.

Tags: #nickelate #superconduct #experimental

Abstract: Identifying the key ingredients for superconductivity under pressure in the Ruddlesden-Popper nickelates remains a formidable challenge, due to a complex interplay between structural variations, oxygen content and location, electronically ordered phases, and the need for high pressures to reach the superconducting phase. To disentangle these complex inter-dependencies, here we study a series of clean single crystals of trilayer La$_4$Ni$_3$O$_{10}$. We discover that enhanced biaxial, compressive pressures induce a zero-resistance state at a 60\% lower pressure compared to previous reports. At the same time, we completely separate the low-pressure density wave phase from superconductivity, effectively ruling out that soft, quantum critical fluctuations of the density wave order parameter act as the pairing glue in this system. Our results establish biaxial, in-plane pressures as a powerful tool for promoting superconductivity in nickelates, unifying the required pressure scales for superconductivity in different Ruddlesden-Popper structures, and providing a connection to the recently discovered thin film samples.

item.description:
Last authors: Takashi Taniguchi, Aaron Sharpe

Authors: Zachary W. Gomez, Nathan Bittner, Jordan T. McCourt, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Autonomous measurement application for graphene and superconductivity materials.

Abstract: Large language model agents have begun to carry out laboratory measurements, but their scientific conclusions are useful only if they hold up under scrutiny. Demonstrating this requires controlled studies because models are stochastic and the context a model is given steers its conclusions. Here we introduce HERA, an autonomous agent designed to carry out cryogenic transport measurements of quantum devices. HERA draws on a knowledge base curated by lab members that holds measurement protocols, software tools, and literature references. We assessed HERA with a blinded trial against an expert on the stacking order of two multilayer graphene devices, an ablation of its knowledge base, and hundreds of offline replays in which models designed the trial's central measurement without running it. These results show that, with a knowledge base designed for the task, language model agents are capable of sound experimental science.

Abstract: Quantum three-wave mixing is an important resource in superconducting quantum circuits. The traditional implementation uses Josephson junction arrays and is activated by magnetic flux. Here we introduce the Berry curvature dipole (BCD) quantum circuit element, which achieves quantum three-wave mixing without breaking time-reversal symmetry. item.description:
Last authors: Yuanyuan Zhao

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Directly related to STS observables in unconventional s+- superconductors and impurity-induced states.

Tags: #theory #superconductivity #STS

Abstract: We study the local Josephson response near nonmagnetic impurities and vortices in a self-consistent two-orbital $s_{\pm}$ superconductor. For a local $s$-wave tip that couples equally to the two orbitals, anomalous spectral contributions of opposite sign nearly cancel in the clean sample. Nonmagnetic impurities redistribute these contributions and can reverse the local coupling without a corresponding $\pi$ phase shift of the bond pair fields. Negative coupling appears at off-center sites at weaker impurity potentials than at the impurity site. The impurity-induced change is concentrated at lower quasiparticle energies, while states over a broader energy range contribute to the total clean and impurity couplings. In zero field, the coupling also changes sign as the tip gap is varied, and increasing the tunneling strength can reverse the $m=1$ sine component of the current without changing the sample state. At the chosen coherence-peak energy, increasing impurity strength mainly changes the relative intensities of existing quasiparticle-interference features. In a self-consistent two-vortex state, the Josephson response develops a spatially varying phase relative to the condensate. The response and condensate share the winding close to each core, while larger loops enclose additional winding of the Josephson response. The local Josephson sign and phase reflect the anomalous spectrum and the tip--sample coupling.

Abstract: We investigate the thermally driven magnon spin current across a junction between a $d$-wave altermagnet (AM) and a ferromagnet (FM) or an antiferromagnet (AFM). For a sublattice-symmetric interface, the two junctions behave oppositely under reversal of the altermagnetic domain: in the FM/AM junction the angularly dependent component is odd and cancels on averaging over the domains, whereas in the AFM/AM junction the angularly independent component vanishes by symmetry and the angularly dependent component survives the domain average at a fixed N\'eel vector of the AFM. Abstract: Multilayer graphenes have emerged as a versatile avenue towards exploring novel electronic phases of matter. Recently, nanoscale multilayer graphene islands have been realized experimentally, where the island is less than 50 nm in diameter and distinct in layer configuration from the contact portion of the same graphene sheets, the latter of which act as leads for transport probes. item.description:
Last authors: Sanjay Rai, Edward Prabu Amaladass

Abstract: Superconducting diode effects are characterized by direction-dependent critical currents in the superconducting state. Here, we investigate diode-like transport in 128-nm-thick Mo thin film deposited on Si_SiO2 substrate by DC magnetron sputtering. The thin film exhibit a superconducting transition temperature TC of 5.8 K. Pronounced current-direction asymmetry and hysteresis are observed in current-voltage characteristics measured in a closed-cycle refrigerator. In contrast, the same thin film exhibits a substantially more symmetric response in a 14T cryogenic system with improved sample thermalization. We attribute this strong dependence on the measurement environment to electrothermal effects arising from current-induced Joule heating and finite thermal relaxation. As the current approaches the superconducting-to-resistive switching condition, the emergence of a resistive component leads to a rapid increase in Joule heating, raising the sample temperature and modifying the switching condition. Conversely, during the resistive-to-superconducting transition, residual heating and finite thermal relaxation reduce the switching current. Since P is equal to I2R it is independent of current polarity, the observed asymmetry is not associated with polarity-dependent Joule heating but with the interplay of thermal relaxation, sweep history, and thermal boundary conditions. The suppression of the asymmetry under improved thermalization, together with similar behavior observed in NbN reference films, indicates that the apparent diode-like response is strongly influenced by electrothermal effects. These results highlight the need to distinguish thermal switching and hysteresis from intrinsic nonreciprocal superconductivity when identifying superconducting diode effects in transport measurements.

item.title: [8] Edge-Plasmon-Induced Magnetization in Higher Chern Insulators
item.description:
Last authors: Thomas L. Schmidt, Eddwi H. Hasdeo

Authors: Prathyush P. Poduval, Rofii, Muhammad S. Ukhtary, Thomas L. Schmidt, Eddwi H. Hasdeo

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Link between Chern number and orbital magnetization at edge states; relevant to topological insulator research.

Abstract: Higher Chern insulators host multiple dissipationless chiral edge states, one per unit of Chern number. We study the collective plasmon modes of these edge states at a domain wall between Chern numbers $\mathcal{C}$ and $-\mathcal{C}$, using a semiclassical model with Coulomb interactions. The plasmon dispersion is linear at long wavelengths, with a velocity that increases linearly with $\mathcal{C}$. As in conventional two-dimensional metals, the edge plasmon generates an elliptically polarized electric field that decays into the bulk and drives electrons in circular orbits, producing a static orbital magnetization (inverse Faraday effect). For topological edge plasmons, the magnetization has a nontrivial spatial profile set by two competing length scales: the finite extent of the edge states and the plasmon wavelength. At fixed edge-charge amplitude, it grows strongly with $\mathcal{C}$. At the domain wall, it approaches a finite plateau at low frequency and decays as $1/\omega^2$ at high frequency. Its temperature dependence is nonmonotonic, with a maximum at an intermediate temperature. These results show how the Chern number controls plasmon-induced magnetization, in contrast to conventional edge plasmons.

item.title: [7] Exceptional Superconducting Interfaces between Graphene and Atomic Chains in A15-MoRe
item.description:
Last authors: Yuichi Ikuhara, Toshiaki Kato

Authors: Hiroto Ogura, Yuto Tsukidate, Shun Kondo, et al.

Why: Investigation of superconducting interfaces involving graphene and Dirac cone hybridization with atomic chains.

Tags: #experiment #graphene #superconductivity

Abstract: Realizing highly transparent and magnetic-field-resilient superconducting contacts is a critical bottleneck for the advancement of two-dimensional (2D) quantum devices. Molybdenum-rhenium (MoRe) alloys have been empirically favored as they uniquely yield ballistic, highly transparent contacts to graphene that survive in high-magnetic-field regimes; however, the microscopic origin of this anomalous transparency has remained a long-standing puzzle. Here, we resolve this paradox by revealing that pristine graphene/MoRe interfaces are governed by the classical A15 superconducting phase. Combining low-temperature transport, X-ray diffraction, and atomic-resolution electron microscopy, we demonstrate that as-deposited MoRe spontaneously forms the A15 phase in direct contact with graphene, whereas thermal annealing triggers a phase transition to a hexagonal close-packed (hcp) structure that severely degrades the Josephson transparency. Crucially, the one-dimensional (1D) transition-metal atomic chains unique to the A15 structure exhibit a near-perfect lattice match (mismatch < 1%) with graphene edges. First-principles calculations further prove that the d-orbitals of these historically renowned 1D chains possibly hybridize with graphene's Dirac cone near the K point. These findings not only uncover the structural and electronic origins of optimal MoRe contacts but also establish A15-phase superconductors as a geometrically ideal, universal platform for realizing robust quantum electronics based on 2D materials.

item.description:
Last authors: Michael Sch\"uler, Samuel Beaulieu

Authors: Sotirios Fragkos, Ann Chantal Goutier, Umberto Dellasette, et al.

Tags: #tr-ARPES #graphene #Floquet #Berrycurvature

Abstract: Driving quantum materials with light can reshape not only their electronic band structures but also the geometry of their electronic wavefunctions. In graphene, circularly polarized light is predicted to open gaps at the Dirac points and induce a pseudospin texture and Berry curvature characteristic of the Haldane model, realizing a Floquet Chern insulator. Transport and all-optical measurements have provided evidence for a light-induced anomalous Hall response, but cannot resolve the underlying electronic states in both energy and momentum space. Time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy has revealed Floquet-Bloch sidebands and hybridization gaps at crossings between Floquet bands. However, these experiments used linearly polarized driving, which preserves time-reversal symmetry and thus does not induce a topological phase. Here, we combine circular-dichroic time-resolved extreme-ultraviolet momentum microscopy with ab initio theory to investigate graphene driven by circularly polarized light. We observe a pump-induced photoemission circular dichroism near the Dirac point that reverses sign with pump helicity and across the Dirac energy, in agreement with our calculations. These results link the measured dichroic response to the light-induced pseudospin texture and its associated Berry curvature, providing spectroscopic evidence for the Floquet-engineered topological insulating state in graphene.

Abstract: Intermixed self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) provide a powerful approach for tuning inorganic-organic interfaces, but their local structure and energetics often remain elusive. Abstract: Disorder plays a central role in correlated quantum materials, but its effects can be highly selective when several electronic orders coexist. Abstract: Multiterminal Josephson junctions have recently attracted substantial attention. Here we turn to the platform of the side-contacted TI trijunction and present experimental evidence for a multiterminal Josephson effect. We study the transport properties and find typical features of a two-dimensional critical current contour (CCC) as well as bias regimes in which only a single junction remains dissipationless. item.title: [7] Spin-Orbit Coupling Response Theory within the Oriented Spin Space Group Framework
item.description:
Last authors: J. Manuel Perez-Mato, Qihang Liu

Authors: Yuntian Liu, Xiaobing Chen, Yutong Yu, Jes\'us Etxebarria, J. Manuel Perez-Mato, Qihang Liu

Why: Symmetry theory for SOC phenomena like the anomalous Hall effect in antiferromagnets.

Tags: #theory #spin-orbit #anomalous-Hall

Abstract: Spin-orbit coupling (SOC) plays a pivotal role in a broad range of phenomena in condensed matter physics. The recently developed spin space group theory offers a new perspective for characterizing the fundamental symmetry-breaking features of SOC-related phenomena, yet its full potential remains to be explored. Here, we provide a general framework that relates the SOC-induced symmetry breaking to modifications of physical properties and emergence of new physical effects. This approach incorporates the recently developed oriented spin space group (OSSG) formalism, which can explicitly describe the symmetry reduction induced by SOC. By parameterizing the SOC Hamiltonian using a SOC tensor that connects real and spin spaces, an expansion in terms of the SOC components can be constructed for the response tensor describing any physical quantity. This framework determines not only whether a SOC-induced response is symmetry allowed, but also the lowest order in SOC at which it emerges and its dependence on magnetic anisotropy. As representative applications, we analyze the magnetoelectric coupling in Type-II multiferroics and show that magnetically induced electric polarization in different systems can be the result of SOC effects of different orders, and can exhibit varying characteristics of magnetic anisotropy. We further apply this theory to the anomalous Hall effect and spin magnetization in antiferromagnets, demonstrating that their distinct transformation properties under the OSSG allow a large anomalous Hall response to coexist with weak spin magnetization. Overall, the proposed framework provides a unified symmetry description of SOC-induced phenomena and offers a systematic way for the identification of SOC-driven functional materials.

item.title: [8] Coexistence of Superconductivity and Chern insulators with |C| 1 in twisted rhombohedral bilayer-trilayer graphene
item.description:
Last authors: Guangyu Zhang, Wei Yang

Authors: Qiu Yang, Zihao Huo, Le Liu, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental report of high Chern number topology and superconductivity in twisted graphene moire.

Tags: #experiment #graphene #topology

Abstract: Rhombohedral multilayer graphene (RMG) has been demonstrated as a promising platform for investigating strongly correlated phases of matter. Here, we observe a coexistence of superconductivity and Chern insulators in a twisted rhombohedral bilayer-trilayer graphene moir\'e superlattice. Superconductivity, evidenced by a sharp transition with a critical temperature of ~180 mK, nonlinear I-V with a BKT temperature of 135 mK, and a signature of phase-sensitive interference patterns, emerges from a symmetry-breaking Fermi surface near v = -2 and D = 0, and it survives at a large in-plane magnetic field up to 2 T, strongly deviating from the Pauli limit. Moreover, we observe a strong modulation of the Ginzburg-Landau coherence length from 467 nm to 145 nm as the in-plane magnetic field increases from 0 to 2 T, whereas the critical current Ic barely changes. Unlike previous studies in RMG, we observe a competition between superconductivity and a correlated insulator at v = -2, monitored by displacement fields and twist angles. Note that we also observe integer Chern insulators with C = 1, 3, and -3 at v = 1/2, 1, and 3, respectively, for large D > 0 in the same superconducting device. The observations establish twisted rhombohedral graphene multilayers as a fascinating system to investigate unconventional superconductivity, high Chern number topology, and their interplay.

item.title: [7] Cage-related crystal-field effects in the paramagnetic range of PrB6
item.description:
Last authors: Christine Opagiste, Natalya Yu. Shitsevalova

Authors: Mehdi Amara, Christine Opagiste, Natalya Yu. Shitsevalova

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Study of crystal-field splitting in the correlated hexaboride PrB6 using neutron scattering.

Tags: #experiment #correlated-electrons #neutron-scattering

Abstract: New insights into the paramagnetic range of PrB$_6$ below 50 K are revealed through specific-heat, thermal-expansion and magnetic measurements. The latent heats of the two successive magnetic transitions, together with an improved description of the lattice contribution, enable a detailed determination of the thermal variation of the magnetic entropy. Immediately above the first-order magnetic ordering temperature ($T_N = 6.7$ K), the magnetic entropy per Pr$^{3+}$ is close to that of a doublet, instead of the triplet crystal-field ground state identified by inelastic neutron scattering. Temperatures in excess of 30 K are required to reach the entropy of the threefold-degenerate ground state. This is reminiscent of the CeB$_6$ case and, similarly, strongly suggests a dynamical splitting of the crystal-field ground state within the boron cage. Further evidence of this splitting is provided by the analysis of the low-temperature paramagnetic susceptibility, which resembles that of a non-magnetic ground state. In addition, a large thermal-expansion anomaly is observed below 20 K, consistent with the expected centrifugal Jahn-Teller effect.

item.description:
Last authors: Weiwei Wang, Jie-Xiang Yu

Authors: Sheng Pan, Weiwei Wang, Jie-Xiang Yu

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical study of MnBi2Te4 switching; relevant to magnetic topological materials.

Tags: #theory #MnBi2Te4 #topology

Abstract: Layer-resolved spin-orbit torques offer a route to controlling antiferromagnetic order through local spin-charge conversion. First-principles calculations show that the layer-resolved spin Hall conductivity of the antiferromagnetic topological insulator $\mathrm{Mn{Bi}_{2}{Te}_{4}}$ consists of a magnetization-independent spin Hall term plus two spin anomalous Hall terms that are even in the N\'eel vector yet evolve with the local magnetic order, while local inversion asymmetry differentiates surface and inner layers. item.description:
Last authors: Jeroen van den Brink, Maia G. Vergniory

Authors: Jorge Cardenas-Gamboa, Devika Jayadeep, Aritz Leonardo, Gregory A. Fiete, Jeroen van den Brink, Maia G. Vergniory

Why: Theoretical route to optically induce altermagnetism in Fe2TeO6; altermagnetism is a key interest.

Abstract: Altermagnets combine compensated collinear magnetic order with momentum-dependent nonrelativistic spin splitting, offering new opportunities for spintronic applications. Here, we propose a route to optically induce altermagnetism through coherent lattice control. Using symmetry analysis, we identify phonon distortions that lift the spin degeneracy of conventional antiferromagnets while preserving the rotational symmetries connecting opposite-spin sublattices. Among these, geometric chiral phonons provide a particularly appealing pathway, linking the emergence of altermagnetism to structural chirality. First-principles-based lattice dynamics reveal the emergence of a transient chiral distortion, while electronic-structure calculations establish that the light-induced structure exhibits nonrelativistic spin splitting characteristic of altermagnetism. Our results establish a symmetry-guided pathway toward the ultrafast optical control of altermagnetic states through nonlinear phononics.

Abstract: Layered A-type antiferromagnetic (AFM) semiconductors offer a unique platform for spintronic devices by combining robust magnetism with gate-tunable semiconducting properties. item.description:
Last authors: Vladislav Poliakov, Leonid Levitov

Authors: Archisman Panigrahi, Vladislav Poliakov, Leonid Levitov

Why: Proposal for STM to detect van Hove singularity pairing; directly relevant to electronic structure spectroscopy.

Tags: #STM #method #superconductivity

Abstract: Van Hove (vH) singularities can enhance superconductivity by generating a large pairing susceptibility. Yet, it remains challenging to experimentally establish whether pairing really occurs near these points. We show that the saddle-point dispersion near a vH point gives rise to a `light-cone' vH-selective behavior of Friedel oscillations, which is drastically different from the familiar concentric circles. Each vH point maps onto its own real-space light-cone sector, allowing STM around a single impurity to measure whether---and how strongly---that saddle-point quasiparticle sector is gapped. A superconducting gap near vH points suppresses the oscillations in the directions corresponding to peaks in the gap function angular dependence, a behavior that provides a signature of vH-related pairing at STM-accessible length scales. This STM protocol, targeting vH superconductivity, is capable of determining whether superconducting pairing emerges near the vH points or elsewhere on the Fermi surface.

item.description:
Last authors: Fengcheng Wu, Xiang Li

Abstract: Fractional quantum Hall systems host strongly correlated topological phases with potential applications in topological quantum computation, yet identifying their microscopic ground states remains challenging because competing phases are often nearly degenerate and Landau-level mixing is difficult to treat. item.title: [7] Quantum Gate Engineering in Superconducting NISQ Platforms: Experimental Methods and Emerging Directions
item.description:
Last authors: 80125, Halima Giovanna Ahmad (Dipartimento di Fisica 'Ettore Pancini'

Authors: Alessandro Sarno (Dipartimento di Fisica 'Ettore Pancini', Universit\`a degli Studi di Napoli 'Federico II', Via Cinthia, et al.

Why: Review of quantum gate engineering in superconducting platforms, covering device physics and materials.; tier capped to C: formal/generic theory watch

Tags: #superconductivity #quantumcomputation #method #review

Abstract: This review aims to provide researchers, experimentalists, and quantum engineers with an updated and technically grounded perspective on the implementation of quantum gates in superconducting NISQ devices. The goal is to establish a comprehensive bridge between theoretical quantum circuit synthesis and its practical, experimental implementation, focusing on superconducting quantum technologies. We systematically examine the diverse landscape of superconducting qubits and processor architectures, ranging from conventional transmons to alternative and unconventional designs, evaluating their unique design trade-offs, connectivity constraints, device physics, and materials impact. Moving from theory to actual implementation, we detail how single- and two-qubit operations are synthesized via microwave-driven and flux-activated pulses. We here present our pulse engineering, wave shaping, calibration workflows, demonstrating how to bridge the gap between abstract gate models and real-world hardware limitations in the direction of a hardware-software co-design framework. To validate these operations, we choose benchmarking methodologies with the purpose to get the more efficient metric for the specific evaluation aspect, including truth tables and quantum process tomography. Therefore, we both discuss the theoretical concepts behind the gate synthesis and show experimental implementation of most fundamental gates by proposing a practical workflow.

item.title: [7] A First-Order Phase Transition in Spin-Imbalanced BCS Theory of Superconductivity
item.description:
Last authors: Marius Lemm, Barbara Roos

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical study of a first-order phase transition in spin-imbalanced BCS superconductivity.

Tags: #superconductivity #theory #BCS

Abstract: We study a translation-invariant BCS functional of superconductivity for a system of spin-$1/2$ fermions with spin-dependent chemical potentials, $\mu_+\neq\mu_-$. Numerical work of Caldas and Mota and analytical work of Freiji, Hainzl, and Seiringer has suggested an unusual first-order phase transition in spin-imbalanced BCS models, in which the normal state becomes globally unstable while remaining locally stable. Here, we prove that a first-order phase transition occurs in such spin-imbalanced BCS functionals. For each sufficiently small fixed spin imbalance and sufficiently low temperature, there is a coexistence coupling $\lambda_{\mathrm{fo}}$ strictly below the linear-stability threshold $\lambda_{\mathrm{lin}}$ of the normal state at which the Cooper pair density exhibits a nonzero jump and the minimized energy has a kink. The methodological insight is a coercivity estimate obtained by decomposing the BCS energy minimization into two parts, where the ``inner'' problem minimizes over the one-particle density matrices at fixed pairing and can be exactly solved by a Legendre--Fenchel transform.

item.title: [8] Fate of Quantum Magic
item.description:
Last authors: Erik S. S{\o}rensen, William Witczak-Krempa

Authors: Liuke Lyu, Erik S. S{\o}rensen, William Witczak-Krempa

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Connects quantum resource 'magic' to quantum materials (Kitaev spin liquid, Ising), proposing neutron scattering experiment.

Tags: #quantuminformation #spinliquid #neutronscattering #stronglycorrelated #theory

Abstract: Magic, a quantum resource distinct from entanglement, measures departure from states stabilized by products of Pauli operators. Such stabilizer states can be maximally entangled yet admit efficient classical description: quantum advantage requires magic. We develop a powerful framework to evaluate the degree of magic in generic many-body states. We use it to study the fate of magic under thermal and dynamical evolution. In the transverse field Ising model, we find a thermal sudden death of magic that saturates with system size, and occurs after the death of entanglement. We reach similar conclusions in generic spin chains, and in the Kitaev quantum spin liquid on the honeycomb lattice, where the threshold shows an intricate dependence on subregion shape. We then study how magic equilibrates after a quantum quench. In quenches of generic spin chains, the magic of a subregion typically dies before entanglement, contrary to thermal trajectories. An explanation is given in terms of the geometry of non-magical states. As a third type of trajectory, we examine the fate of magic with separation with an appropriate notion of non-local magic and establish a sudden death. Finally, we show how to experimentally witness a volume law of frame-robust magic in quantum materials by using neutron scattering.

item.title: [7] Electrochemical functionalization of graphene rationalized by Hammett and Swain-Lupton parameters
item.description:
Last authors: C. Sevik, L. F. Vega, F. M. Peeters, M. Lozada-Hidalgo

Authors: L. Chen, H. Li, C. Li, X. Zhang, Q. Dai, M. Alhashmi, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of electronic properties and functionalization of monolayer graphene.

Tags: #graphene #monolayer #electrochemistry #electronicproperties #experiment

Abstract: Graphene's sp^{2}-bonded carbon lattice makes it exceptionally resistant to covalent functionalization, with existing approaches relying on chemically specific and often harsh methods, fragmenting our understanding of its reactivity. Here we show that electric fields of approximately 1 V nm^{-1} in non-aqueous electrolytes enable the electrochemical functionalization of monolayer graphene with a broad range of substituents, leading to two-order-of-magnitude conductance modulation stable over 5,000 cycles and semi-reversible electronic conductor-insulator transitions. Analysis of the oxidation potentials across substituents reveals trends governed by classical descriptors. Species forming localised {\sigma} bonds display increasing oxidation potentials with the meta-Hammett constant ({\sigma}_m), whereas substituents interacting via delocalised {\pi} orbitals follow an inverse dependence on the modified Swain-Lupton resonance parameter (R). These relationships indicate that graphene's oxidation potential increases with the electron-withdrawing strength of the substituent. Our results provide new insights into the electrochemical activity of inert materials under strong electric fields.

item.title: [8] Quantum noise spectroscopy of superconducting dynamics in a cuprate thin film
item.description:
Last authors: Shubhayu Chatterjee, Chong Zu

Authors: Zhongyuan Liu, Ruotian Gong, Jaewon Kim, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: NV sensing of nodal quasiparticles in BSCCO; directly relevant to cuprate electronic structure.

Tags: #method #material #superconductivity #cuprate

Abstract: Characterizing the low-energy dynamics of quantum materials is crucial for understanding strongly correlated electronic states, yet remains experimentally challenging, particularly in two-dimensional systems. Here, we leverage nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond as a non-invasive quantum sensor to study thin-film Bi$_2$Sr$_2$CaCu$_2$O$_{8+\delta}$ (BSCCO), revealing several distinct dynamical phenomena across the superconducting phase diagram. At zero magnetic field and low temperatures, NV depolarization ($T_1$) spectroscopy captures GHz-scale noise from nodal quasiparticle excitations, consistent with Bardeen--Cooper--Schrieffer (BCS) mean-field theory. Near the critical temperature $T_c \approx 90$ K, supercurrent-fluctuation-induced noise sharply reduces $T_1$. By analyzing the temperature scaling of $T_1$, we observe clear deviations from mean-field prediction, reflecting the importance of order parameter fluctuations and enabling the determination of critical exponents. Under a small magnetic field, a broad and asymmetric reduction of $T_1$ unveils a liquid-like phase of mobile vortices. NV decoherence ($T_2$) spectroscopy further probes MHz-scale noise and reveals complex vortex-solid fluctuations well below $T_c$. Our results establish quantum noise spectroscopy as a non-invasive probe of superconducting dynamics over frequency and length scales complementary to existing techniques.

Abstract: We show that the quantum geometry of fractionalized spin excitations in Mott-insulating quantum spin liquids (QSL) gives rise to a finite Raman circular dichroism (RCD) signal. We identify conditions under which the Loudon--Fleury framework, where light modulates the underlying exchange interactions, and the light-matter-coupling approach, where the effective vector potential couples directly to the spinon bands, yield equivalent Raman vertices for the fractionalized quasiparticles. item.title: [8] Thermal Strain-Driven Periodic Ripples in Ultrathin Sb2Te3/Graphene Heterostructures and their Implications for Strain Engineering
item.description:
Last authors: Valentina Gallardo, Carolina Parra

Authors: Francisco Munoz, Manuel Fuenzalida, Paula Mellado, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Examines band structure modifications in TI/graphene vdW heterostructures due to periodic ripples.

Tags: #material #vanderWaals #topologicalinsulator #graphene

Abstract: We report the observation of a highly regular, periodic ripple superstructure with a characteristic wavelength of approximately 8.7 nm in a van der Waals heterostructure composed of ultrathin Sb2Te3 epitaxially grown on monolayer graphene. We attribute this structural modulation to an extrinsic, thermally driven mechanism: upon post-growth cooling, the opposite signs of the thermal expansion coefficients of the bulk SiO2 substrate and the graphene layer generate interfacial strain that drives the formation of ripples. In this ultrathin thickness regime, the Sb2Te3 film conforms to the buckled graphene morphology without delamination, because the interfacial van der Waals adhesion energy exceeds the elastic energy cost associated with bending. This substrate-induced templating mechanism is expected to be broadly applicable to other two-dimensional materials grown on graphene, provided that they are sufficiently thin to remain mechanically coupled below a critical bending thickness. Furthermore, based on density functional theory and effective low-energy model calculations, we predict that this structural corrugation leads to substantial modifications of the electronic band structure. The resulting periodic ripple potential suppresses the trivial hybridization gap in the planar configuration and transforms the spinless Dirac-Dirac resonance into a gapless helical metallic state with a dense, nontrivial spin texture.

Abstract: The ultrastrong coupling regime of cavity photons and quantum materials has emerged as a pathway to modify materials properties, however definitive signatures of ultrastrong coupling remain elusive. Focusing on the quantum photon statistics of light transmitted through a cavity-embedded superconductor, we show that a two-photon Higgs polariton at strong coupling realizes a photonic nonlinearity at the single terahertz photon level. We find that as light-matter coupling increases, the photon statistics show pronounced changes due to the formation of a hybrid photon-matter dark-cavity state with finite photon occupancy, producing testable signatures of ultrastrong coupling. We derive a non-Markovian input output relation and study the cavity-embedded superconductor 2H-NbSe2 as it approaches ultrastrong light-matter coupling. Our results reveal a diagnostic for ultrastrong coupling in the two-photon coincidence statistics that is absent in total counts.

item.description:
Last authors: Dieter Koelle, Wolfgang Lang

Abstract: Focused helium ion beam (He-FIB) irradiation with 30-keV ions is a key tool for nanoscale patterning and defect engineering in high transition temperature (Tc) cuprate superconducting devices, yet its usable fluence window is constrained by the competing requirements of reliable superconductivity suppression and minimal structural degradation. Raman spectra exhibit increasing disorder while lacking signatures of oxygen depletion, indicating that irradiation mainly generates oxygen-related Frenkel defects rather than changing the carrier concentration. Consistently, with increasing fluence, the normal-state resistivity \rho_N(T) at temperature T above Tc increases strongly, while d \rho_N/d T remains nearly unchanged at moderate fluence. The suppression of Tc is accurately described by Abrikosov-Gor'kov pair breaking and reaches complete quenching of superconductivity at 4.5 x 10^15 cm^-2. The anisotropic upper critical fields decrease approximately exponentially with increasing fluence, the vortex activation energy is reduced, and the anisotropy drops, in contrast to oxygen-depleted YBCO. Hall-angle analysis confirms a nearly constant carrier density but a systematic increase in defect scattering and reduced mobility, consistent with a crossover toward the dirty limit at high fluence. item.description:
Last authors: Massimo Capone, Nicola Marzari

Authors: Matteo Quinzi, Andrea Pintus, Tommaso Chiarotti, Massimo Capone, Nicola Marzari

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Relevant to pseudogap physics in correlated systems, connecting real-space textures to momentum-space spectral features.

Tags: #correlated #pseudogap #Hubbard

Abstract: Strongly correlated solids exhibit phenomena -- from Mott localization to high-temperature superconductivity -- that escape conventional band theory. Efforts to address this unconventional physics have been typically cast in the language of Green's function theories, with the associated self-energies capturing strong correlations beyond the reach of mean-field theories. Here, we underscore that frequency- and momentum-dependent self-energies emerge also from mean-field solutions that break translational symmetry, and that these self-energies can display the characteristic fingerprints of strong correlations for certain, physically meaningful, spatial patterns. In the paradigmatic case of the 2D Hubbard model, we find that already at the mean-field level the doped antiferromagnet develops, in addition to long-range ordered stripes, many quasi-degenerate self-consistent solutions with antiferromagnetic textures organized into antiphase domains separated by hole-rich interfaces of convoluted shape, reminiscent of the phase-separation scenario. Remarkably, these solutions map into spectral functions that display very distinctively the phenomenology of the pseudogap, including the nodal-antinodal dichotomy, Fermi arcs, and a complementary Luttinger surface. The result is a conceptually simple description of such a complex phenomenon, where a pseudogap emerges as the momentum-space spectral portrait of the real-space interplay between antiferromagnetic domains and their metallic interfaces.

item.description:
Last authors: Qiang Gao, Taige Wang

Why: Computational method to address long-standing fractional quantum Hall challenges in the thermodynamic limit.

Abstract: Determining correlated ground states directly in the thermodynamic limit remains a central challenge in quantum many-body physics. Here we develop a quantum many-body bootstrap that yields a rigorous and tight lower bound on the thermodynamic ground-state energy of a fractional quantum Hall system together with an optimized reduced density matrix $ ho_W^\star$ on a spatial window. For sufficiently tight bounds, we find that $ ho_W^\star$ accurately reproduces the ground-state reduced density matrix, as directly tested by its fidelity with known model states. For exactly solvable Laughlin and Moore--Read parent Hamiltonians, the bootstrap also reproduces pair correlations and orbital entanglement spectra (OES). For Landau-level-projected Coulomb interactions across multiple fillings, the energy bounds closely track established thermodynamic estimates, while the window density matrix recovers the familiar $ u=1/3$ Laughlin and $ u=5/2$ Moore--Read states and the composite Fermi liquid at $ u=1/2$. More importantly, the same framework also resolves unsettled regimes. At $ u=1/4$, the OES and real-space correlations identify a composite Fermi liquid, while at $ u=12/5$ the combined diagnostics suggest $\overline{\mathrm{RR}}_3$ as the ground-state order. Our bootstrap therefore provides direct access to both ground-state energies and many-body structure in the thermodynamic limit.

item.title: [7] Collinear and Coplanar Altermagnetism in a Penrose Quasicrystal
item.description:
Last authors: Ye Cao, Fan Yang

Authors: Bai-He Yao, Zhi-Yan Shao, Ye Cao, Fan Yang

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Investigates altermagnetism with direct mention of ARPES signatures, a key interest area.

Tags: #altermagnet #photoemission #Hubbard

Abstract: We generalize the previous group-theory based classification of collinear magnetism in the quasicrystal (QC) to general magnetic states. Taking the Penrose lattice as an example, we find that the magnetic states corresponding to 2D irreducible representations (IRRPs) of the $D_5$ point group represent for a new type of altermagnetism (AM). Unlike conventional AM wherein zero magnetism is protected by, e.g. rotation or mirror reflection, which globally flips the spin in the magnetic pattern, the zero magnetism in these 2D-IRRP states is instead protected by a special group-representation-orthogonality theorem which states that basis functions belonging to different IRRPs are mutually orthogonal. This special compensation mechanism and the absence of $\mathcal{PT}$ symmetry finally lead to AM states. Taking the Penrose-Hubbard model as an example, our linear-response theory and Ginzburg-Landau theory based analysis show that the largest portion of the parameter space is occupied by such 2D-IRRP states, which can be either collinear or coplanar AM states. These special AM states are characterized by spin split in the spin-resolved angular-resolved photoemission spectroscopy and the spin conductance with unique symmetry features. These intriguing collinear and coplanar AM states result from symmetry and can also emerge in other QCs.

item.title: [7] The bulk spectral gap is certifiable from above but uncomputable from below
item.description:
Last authors: Omar Fawzi, Marc-Olivier Renou

Authors: Xiangling Xu, Matthias Sch\"otz, Jie Wang, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical work on spectral gaps in many-body systems, directly applies to kagome Heisenberg antiferromagnet.

Tags: #theory #kagome #antiferromagnet #quantum_many_body_physics

Abstract: Determining spectral gaps in the thermodynamic limit is a central challenge in quantum many-body physics. When a fixed boundary condition is imposed, this problem is undecidable: no algorithm, even with unlimited resources, can decide for every Hamiltonian whether it is gapped. Yet the thermodynamic limit is meant to capture the intrinsic properties of very large systems, which should not depend on how their boundaries are chosen. We therefore consider the bulk spectral gap, which concerns only the intrinsic excitations of the infinite system, and ask what can and cannot be computed about it. First, we give a general algorithm producing a hierarchy of certified upper bounds on the bulk gap, arbitrarily tight at the cost of more computation. Second, we prove that the spectral gap problem remains undecidable in the bulk, already for translationally invariant nearest-neighbour chains of fixed local dimension. Hence no general algorithm produces convergent lower bounds, and no convergent upper-bounding algorithm, ours included, admits a computable convergence rate. The bulk spectral gap is thus certifiable from above but uncomputable from below; more precisely, the bulk-gaplessness promise problem is RE-complete, exactly as hard as the halting problem. The same construction shows that no general algorithm can decide whether a given product state is a ground state, and that convergent bounds on ground-state expectation values admit no computable convergence rate in general. Finally, we obtain the first nontrivial certified upper bounds on the bulk gap of the spin-1/2 kagome Heisenberg antiferromagnet.
